question: Which IPv6 bind contract should OpenClaw expose for Gateway LAN/custom mode?
rationale: The central implementation choice changes non-loopback Gateway exposure and upgrade semantics, and repository policy treats config/default/startup behavior plus security boundaries as maintainer decisions rather than automatic repair work.

options.title: Add explicit dual-stack opt-in
options.body: Introduce a documented IPv6 or dual-stack bind contract with security warnings, platform listener semantics, and fresh-install/upgrade proof.

options.title: Change LAN/custom in place
options.body: Make existing `lan` or `customBindHost` accept IPv6 directly, accepting the compatibility and global IPv6 exposure risk as the new behavior for those modes.

options.title: Keep IPv4-only core
options.body: Leave core bind behavior IPv4-only and continue documenting reverse-proxy or sidecar workarounds for IPv6-only platforms.

recommendation.title: Add explicit dual-stack opt-in
recommendation.body: Introduce a documented IPv6 or dual-stack bind contract with security warnings, platform listener semantics, and fresh-install/upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal for the affected Gateway network resolver and IPv6 loopback behavior points to this owner candidate.
